title: Pointwise smoothness from a smooth fibre
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], let $x\in X$ and $s=f(x)$. Assume the local ring map $\mathcal O_{S,s}\to\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism]. Then $f$ is smooth at $x$ (there is an open neighbourhood of $x$ on which $f$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]) if and only if the fibre morphism $X_s\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre, def-weil-residue-field] is smooth at the point corresponding to $x$.

proof.text: Suppose $f$ is smooth on an open neighbourhood $U$ of $x$. Apply [sbc-lem-smooth-criterion] to $f|_U:U\to S$: its fibre $U_s\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ is smooth. By [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product], $U_s$ identifies with the open subscheme of $X_s$ lying above $U$, compatibly with the morphism to $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$. This open contains the point corresponding to $x$ by [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. It is therefore the required smooth neighbourhood in the fibre.

Conversely suppose $X_s\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ is smooth at $x$. By [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] choose affine neighbourhoods $W=\operatorname{Spec}A\subset X$ of $x$ and $V=\operatorname{Spec}R\subset S$ of $s$, with $f(W)\subset V$ and $A$ finitely presented over $R$. Write $\varphi:R\to A$ for the induced map and $\mathfrak q\subset A$ for $x$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-induced-ring-map-spec-square], $\mathfrak p=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$ represents $s$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization] and [lem-weil-pbc-spec-map-stalk-localization], the local map $R_{\mathfrak p}\to A_{\mathfrak q}$ is the given stalk map under ring isomorphisms. It is flat by hypothesis; no flatness away from $x$ is asserted.

source.place: Tag 01V9, lemma-smooth-at-point, affine reduction for (2) implies (1); Algebra Tag 00TF hypotheses (1) and (2)

proof.text: With these affine charts, apply [lem-trf-smooth-fibre-affine-ring-at-prime] to the assumed smooth fibre neighbourhood. For $k=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ and $F=A\otimes_R k$, it gives that $k\to F$ is smooth at $\mathfrak Q=\ker(F\to\kappa(\mathfrak q))$, exactly the prime used in the ring fibre criterion.

source.place: Tag 01V9, lemma-smooth-at-point, proof of (2) implies (1): affine translation of the smooth-fibre hypothesis before applying Algebra lemma-flat-fibre-smooth.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-smooth-fibre-smooth-at-prime] to $\varphi:R\to A$, $\mathfrak p$, and $\mathfrak q$. Its finite-presentation condition holds with the element $1\notin\mathfrak q$ because $A$ is finitely presented over $R$ (step 2). Its local-flatness condition is step 2, and its smooth-fibre condition is step 3, with precisely the kernel prime $\mathfrak Q$ specified in its statement. It follows that $R\to A$ is smooth at $\mathfrak q$.

source.place: Tag 01V9, lemma-smooth-at-point, (2) implies (1) by Algebra Tag 00TF, lemma-flat-fibre-smooth

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-affine-smooth-prime-scheme-neighbourhood] to $f$, the same charts $W,V$, and the smoothness of $R\to A$ at $\mathfrak q$ just proved. It supplies $g\notin\mathfrak q$ and a principal open neighbourhood $W_g$ of $x$ with $f|_{W_g}:W_g\to S$ smooth. This is smoothness of $f$ at $x$.
